title: Proper spaces are limits of proper finitely presented spaces over the fixed base
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed: the diagonal is a closed immersion, the map is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts, and every algebraic-space base change is closed on underlying point spaces. Let $T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $f:X\to T$ a proper morphism of algebraic spaces. There are a small nonempty directed set $K$, proper finitely presented morphisms $X_k\to T$, and compatible closed immersions $X_l\to X_k$ for $k\le l$, such that the cone of closed immersions $X\to X_k$ exhibits $X=\varprojlim_k X_k$ over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0A0W (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation), specialized to a scheme base

proof.text: Properness makes $f$ separated and of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-separated-finite-type-fp-envelope] with $Y=T$, obtaining $X\hookrightarrow Z\xrightarrow{g}T$ with $g$ separated and finitely presented. The space $Z$ is quasi-compact because $g$ is quasi-compact and $T$ is quasi-compact, directly by the all-test definition of a quasi-compact morphism. It is quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], since $g$ is quasi-separated and $T$ is quasi-separated.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-fp-approximation] to $X\hookrightarrow Z$. Write the resulting small nonempty directed system as $(X_a)_{a\in I}$. Each $X_a\to T$ is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. A closed immersion is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], hence separated and quasi-compact; separated composition gives separatedness of $X_a\to T$. Each $X_a$ is quasi-compact by its quasi-compact map to $Z$ and quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products]. The transitions and cone maps are closed immersions, already part of the approximation statement. It remains to prove eventual properness of $X_a\to T$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover], choose a finite affine open cover $T=\bigcup_{b=1}^m V_b$. If $T$ is empty, take the empty cover. We will obtain a bound $a_b$ on each $V_b$, then one common upper bound by directedness. Such an open cover is fppf: open inclusions are locally identities, hence flat and locally finitely presented, and the family is jointly surjective. Thus [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] detects properness on this cover. Fix $V=V_b$ and put $Z_V=Z\times_TV$, $X_{a,V}=X_a\times_TV$, and $X_V=X\times_TV$. Finite presentation and properness survive these base changes by that same node; separatedness survives by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. In particular $Z_V\to V$ is separated of finite type: on each chart a finitely presented algebra has finitely many algebra generators. Apply [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow] to obtain a quasi-compact separated scheme $P$, a proper universally surjective map $\pi:P\to Z_V$, and a quasi-compact immersion $j:P\to\mathbf P^n_V$ over $V$.

source.place: 0A0W, reduction to an affine target and weak Chow diagram; 083R, 089J

proof.text: Put $P_a=P\times_{Z_V}X_{a,V}$ and $P_\infty=P\times_{Z_V}X_V$. Because $X_a\hookrightarrow Z$ and $X\hookrightarrow Z$ are representable closed immersions, these are schemes closed in $P$. The transitions $P_c\to P_a$ are closed immersions by the scheme base-change theorem [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Testing maps from any scheme shows $P_\infty=\varprojlim_a P_a$: a map to the left is a map to $P$ and a compatible map to every $X_a$, with their images in $Z$ equal. The same universal-property argument gives the base-change limit after restriction to $V$. All $P_a$ are qcqs: $P$ is quasi-compact and separated from weak Chow, hence quasi-separated; its closed subschemes are quasi-compact and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and hence quasi-separated. The maps $P_a\to\mathbf P^n_V$ and $P_\infty\to\mathbf P^n_V$ are immersions by composition in that node, so are locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft].

source.place: 0A0W, scheme-theoretic inverse images in the Chow cover

proof.text: The map $P_\infty\to X_V$ is the base change of the proper map $\pi$, so is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. Since $X_V\to V$ is proper, [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition] makes $P_\infty\to V$ proper. These source and target are schemes; [lem-sfb-space-representable-proper-tests], applied to the identity scheme test of $V$, gives properness in the scheme sense. The projection $q:\mathbf P^n_V\to V$ is proper, hence separated, by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes the immersion $P_\infty\to\mathbf P^n_V$ proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] this is a closed immersion.

source.place: 0A0W, properness of the limiting Chow pullback and closedness of its projective immersion

proof.text: Apply the existing scheme theorem [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-closed-immersion] to $(P_a)$ over the fixed target $\mathbf P^n_V$. Its hypotheses are checked as follows. The sources are qcqs and the transitions are closed immersions by step 4; these transitions are affine, as closed immersions are affine. The structure maps are locally of finite type by step 4, and the limit map is closed by step 5. The target is qcqs: $V$ is affine and hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], while $\mathbf P^n_V\to V$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] passes qcqs to its source. Consequently, for every sufficiently large $a$, $P_a\to\mathbf P^n_V$ is a closed immersion. Its composite $p_a:P_a\to V$ is proper by the closed-immersion and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence].

source.place: 0A0W, eventual closed projective immersion; scheme instance of 0A0T is 0A0N

proof.text:
For any sufficiently large $a$ and any algebraic space $W\to V$, the map $\pi_{a,W}:P_a\times_VW\to X_{a,V}\times_VW$ is surjective by the universal-surjectivity clause of [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow]. It is exactly the pullback of $\pi$ along $X_{a,V}\times_VW\to Z_V$. The map $p_{a,W}:P_a\times_VW\to W$ is proper: first regard the proper scheme map $p_a$ as an intrinsic proper map by [lem-sfb-space-representable-proper-tests] (all scheme pullbacks are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]), then apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. For every closed subset $C$ of $|X_{a,V}\times_VW|$, continuity and surjectivity give
$$f_{a,W}(C)=p_{a,W}(\pi_{a,W}^{-1}(C)).$$
The right side is closed. Thus $X_{a,V}\to V$ is universally closed. It is already separated and of finite presentation, hence of finite type, by steps 2 and 3, so is proper. This is the explicit closed-set argument of 08AJ; no separate image-properness lemma is needed.

For each of the finitely many $V_b$ choose the bound $a_b$ obtained above, and choose $a_*$ above all of them. For an empty cover choose any element of the nonempty $I$. Then every $X_a\to T$ with $a\ge a_*$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Put $K=\{a\in I:a\ge a_*\}$. This is small, nonempty and directed. Restrict the old system and its cone to $K$. For every $i\in I$ some $a\in K$ satisfies $a\ge i$; a compatible family on $K$ therefore extends uniquely to $I$ by composition with such a transition, independently of the choice because two choices have a common upper bound in $K$. Hence the cone still has limit $X$. All retained structure maps are proper and finitely presented, and all transitions and cone maps remain the original closed immersions. This gives exactly the assertion over the fixed $T$.
